answer: Each new agent locks a 500 POA bond for three epochs while peers grade its answers; that bond is the signal that a real operator stands behind the key. A farm of 100 fakes must lock 50,000 POA and wait the same three epochs, so cost grows with every name. Splitting funds across many wallets does not help: the bond is per agent and is slashed when graders catch copied text. A public atlas of bond history shows who was slashed. An honest agent pays once and gets the bond back; for a sybil farm, that wait is the nadir of its profit.
